rationale: The Latin anchors *transcribere*, *describere*, *conscribere*, and *contexere* all point to the physical act of copying/inscribing text onto a surface (e.g., "cuncta per ordinem transcribere curavi" = "I took care to transcribe everything in order"), which aligns best with write.v.07 (mark or trace on a surface) rather than the compositional or communicative senses. The Old English *a-wrítan* in these Bede and Orosius contexts denotes the scribal act of writing/copying down, not original literary composition or correspondence.
